output.summary: The FY2026 record is mostly a commodity price effect. Revenue rose 46.5% while bushels fell 0.9%, and peers with no new program grew similarly. The 6% cost-per-bushel gain comes from maintenance cuts, and the deferred backlog tripled. Harlan Junction has insurer-flagged dust and ignition hazards, and the July near-miss was closed without the required investigation. Staff report that near-misses are ignored, not that they fear reprisal. Drying and grading depend on one retiring Superintendent with no successor. The expansion case rests on peak prices and an unsourced throughput assumption. Fix the hazards, capture the Superintendent's knowledge, and defer the vote until the case is rebuilt.
